title: Infographics
slide_intent: Show designers how to give evidence enough structure to read. Charts, labels and illustrations have distinct jobs when a reader needs to compare quantities.
strategic_value: Frontline AIDS can carry its illustrated language into reporting while retaining conventional charts for quantitative comparisons.
demonstration: The upper example combines pictograms, a globe, bars and circular indicators. The lower row isolates charts and percentage devices without the full illustrative setting.
practical_value: Use the simpler treatment for data that needs context or close comparison. Keep illustrations sparse where competing shapes would distract from quantities.
